events.text: The first Super Bowl is played in Los Angeles
Uruguay hosts the first FIFA World Cup
Riders set off on the first Tour de France
The All England Club holds the first Wimbledon Championship

reveal.explanation: Wimbledon began in 1877 as a way to pay for a broken lawn roller, and the Tour de France was dreamed up in 1903 to sell newspapers. The World Cup followed in 1930, and the first Super Bowl, known at the time as the AFL–NFL World Championship Game, was played in 1967.

sources.excerpt: The 1877 Wimbledon Championship was a men's tennis tournament held at the All England Croquet and Lawn Tennis Club (AEC & LTC) in Wimbledon, London. It was the world's first official lawn tennis tournament, and was later recognised as the first Grand Slam tournament or "Major".
The 1903 Tour de France was the first cycling race set up and sponsored by the newspaper L'Auto, ancestor of the current daily, L'Équipe.
The 1930 FIFA World Cup was the first FIFA World Cup, the world championship for men's national football teams. It took place in Uruguay from 13 to 30 July 1930.

The first AFL–NFL World Championship Game (known retroactively as Super Bowl I and referred to in contemporaneous reports, including the game's radio broadcast, as the Super Bowl) was an American football game played on January 15, 1967, at the Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Los Angeles, California.

editorNotes: Wimbledon is dated by the tournament played in July 1877, not the club's founding in 1868 or the introduction of lawn tennis there in 1875. The Tour de France was announced in January 1903 and raced that July, so the year is unaffected. The first Super Bowl was played on 15 January 1967 and was officially the AFL–NFL World Championship Game; the article notes contemporary reports already called it the Super Bowl, so the familiar name is used.
